title: Hello and Goodbye
subtitle: おはよう・またね
review: Written by Claude. The Japanese, the romaji and the humor have not been checked by a Japanese speaker. English support only: no Burmese lines yet.
intro: Good morning at noon, a trip to the convenience store in pajamas, a husband who comes home still talking to his colleagues, and a long goodbye between two people who live together: four short scenes between Emi and Riku. Listen for which greeting goes with which moment, and for what happens when someone picks the wrong one.

lines.note: Konnichiwa is for the daytime. Emi is telling him the morning is over.

lines.romaji: Jūniji da yo. Hisashiburi. Genki datta?
lines.kana: じゅうにじだよ。ひさしぶり。げんきだった？
lines.say: 十二時だよ。久しぶり。元気だった？

tr.en: It's twelve. Long time no see. How have you been?

lines.note: Hisashiburi is for someone you have not seen for a long time. Here it is a joke.

lines.kana: じゃあ…おはようございます。
lines.note: Gozaimasu makes ohayō polite. It does not make it morning.

lines.romaji: Teinei ni itte mo, mō hiru da yo.
lines.kana: ていねいにいっても、もうひるだよ。
lines.say: 丁寧に言っても、もう昼だよ。

tr.en: Saying it politely doesn't help. It's already noon.

lines.note: Teinei: polite. Mō: already. Hiru: noon, daytime.
Oyasumi: what you say to someone who is going to bed. Polite: oyasuminasai.
Said when you leave home. Literally: I'll go and come back.

lines.kana: いってらっしゃい。きをつけてね。
lines.say: 行ってらっしゃい。気をつけてね。
lines.note: Itterasshai is the answer of the person who stays. Ki o tsukete: take care.

lines.romaji: Un. Konbini ni iku dake da yo.
lines.kana: うん。コンビニにいくだけだよ。
lines.say: うん。コンビニに行くだけだよ。

tr.en: Yeah. I'm only going to the convenience store.

lines.note: Un: a casual yes. Dake: only.
Kakkō: what you look like, your outfit.
Said when you come home, however short the trip.

lines.kana: おかえり。はやかったね。
lines.note: Okaeri answers tadaima. Polite: okaerinasai.

lines.kana: おかえり。おそかったね。
lines.note: Osoi: late. Osokatta: was late.

tr.en: Thank you for your hard work.

lines.note: What colleagues say to each other at work, all day long. Not what you say to your wife.

lines.romaji: … Koko wa kaisha ja nai yo.
lines.kana: …ここはかいしゃじゃないよ。
lines.note: Kaisha: company, office. Ja nai: is not.
A formal apology. Riku is still in office mode.

lines.kana: だいじょうぶ？つかれてる？

tr.en: Are you OK? Are you tired?

lines.romaji: Hai. Dewa, osaki ni shitsurei shimasu.
lines.kana: はい。では、おさきにしつれいします。
lines.say: はい。では、お先に失礼します。

tr.en: Yes. Well then, excuse me for leaving before you.

lines.note: What you say when you leave the office before your colleagues. He means: I'm going to bed.

lines.kana: おつかれさまでした。おやすみ。
lines.say: お疲れ様でした。おやすみ。

tr.en: Thank you for your hard work. Good night.

lines.note: Otsukaresama deshita is the correct office reply. Emi gives up and plays along.
Mata: again. Ashita: tomorrow.
Mo: too. Japanese often uses the name where English says 'you'.
Ano: um. It gets someone's attention gently.

lines.romaji: Bokutachi, onaji ie ni kaeru yo ne.
lines.kana: ぼくたち、おなじいえにかえるよね。
lines.say: 僕たち、同じ家に帰るよね。

tr.en: We're going home to the same house, aren't we?

lines.note: Onaji: the same. Yo ne asks the other person to confirm.
Sō datta: that's right, I had forgotten.

notes: By time of day: ohayō in the morning, konnichiwa in the daytime, konbanwa in the evening, oyasumi at bedtime.
To be polite, add to the casual form: ohayō gozaimasu, oyasuminasai, okaerinasai.
Home greetings come in pairs. Leaving: ittekimasu, then itterasshai. Coming back: tadaima, then okaeri.
Office greetings: otsukaresama desu all day long; osaki ni shitsurei shimasu when you leave first; otsukaresama deshita in reply.
Between friends: ja, mata ne; mata ashita; bai bai. Sayōnara is rare in daily life: it sounds like a long goodbye.
Casual speech drops desu and masu and ends in yo, ne or yo ne: hiru da yo, hayakatta ne, kaeru yo ne.

questions.q: It is twelve o'clock. Which greeting fits?
questions.why: Konnichiwa is for the daytime. Ohayō is for the morning.

questions.q: Riku says: Ittekimasu! What does Emi answer?
questions.why: Ittekimasu and itterasshai go together when someone leaves home.

questions.q: Riku comes back and says: Tadaima. What does Emi answer?
questions.why: Tadaima and okaeri go together when someone comes home.

questions.q: Where do people say: Osaki ni shitsurei shimasu?
options: At the office, when leaving first
questions.why: It excuses you for leaving before your colleagues. Riku uses it to go to bed.

questions.q: Why is 'Mata ashita' funny in the last scene?
options: Emi and Riku live in the same house.
It is only for the morning.
questions.why: Mata ashita = see you tomorrow. They are going home together.
